decision_lens: Prioritize findings by whether they change the truth value of 'nobody is auditing arenas' — a single credible counterexample (an existing tool, paper, or standard practice that does what SPAN/ARTIFACT do under another name) undermines the uniqueness claim more than any number of positioning refinements.
focus: Whether 'nobody is auditing arenas' is true across the actual LLM-agent-benchmark ecosystem — DF-agent repos, WebArena/OSWorld/tau-bench/SWE-bench-class arenas, and RL-environment engineering practice — or whether equivalent checks already exist under different names with different distribution.
name: fd-agentarena-audit-landscape
persona: Apply the perspective of an agent-benchmark and RL-environment engineering specialist with working knowledge of the WebArena/OSWorld/tau-bench/SWE-bench-class benchmark ecosystem, gym/environment design practice, and the RL literature on reward hacking, environment bugs, and control-policy sanity checks — someone who has built or maintained a long-horizon agent evaluation harness and knows what practitioners in this space already check by convention versus what they skip.
review_areas: Named-precedent search: check whether 'control policies' / 'no-op baselines' / 'oracle policies' — standard practice in RL benchmark papers (Atari/ALE, MiniHack, Crafter, NetHack Learning Environment) and in some agent benchmarks (WebArena's human-trajectory upper bound, SWE-bench's gold-patch reference) — already do what SPAN claims to originate, and flag where the doc's 'nobody' claim doesn't survive naming them.

fort-gym as the strongest counter-example: the doc says fort-gym 'independently rediscovered' rules 2, 5, 6 but has 'no sign of' SPAN/ARTIFACT on a grep-only read — stress whether a full read (not grep) would find the equivalent under different naming, since a grep-level competitive claim is exactly the kind of undercooked evidence the doc itself would flag if applied to fort-bench.

Distribution/demand test: assess whether arena-auditing tooling already exists but has no distribution — survey whether adjacent RL/agent-benchmark communities have published (blog posts, workshop papers, GitHub issues) equivalent complaints about benchmark validity that went nowhere, which would support 'no demand' over 'no gap' as the real explanation.

SPAN/ARTIFACT outside a scripted-optimal-policy world: for each of the four named comparison classes (WebArena, OSWorld, tau-bench, SWE-bench-like), assess concretely whether a scripted-optimal policy or a content-preserving permutation is constructible at all — WebArena tasks are often judged by a rubric/functional-correctness checker, tau-bench uses policy-conversation matching, SWE-bench uses test pass/fail; check whether SPAN's question is even well-posed outside a simulated-world arena like fort-bench.

Base-rate check on the 134-repo claim: interrogate whether '134 repos, 9 DF-specific, none auditing' is a meaningful denominator — most agent-benchmark repos of any kind are unmaintained forks or single-author demos, so 'none audits' may be true but uninformative if none of the 134 were ever going to be rigorous regardless of the audit gap.

Reward-hacking / environment-bug literature as prior art: check whether the six killed claims map onto already-catalogued RL environment failure modes (partial observability bugs, reward misspecification, off-by-one termination conditions) documented in existing RL debugging guides, which would mean the methodology itself has partial precedent zahro doesn't cite.

severity_examples.condition: The precedent generalizes beyond fort-bench's specific setup the way SPAN/ARTIFACT claim to.
severity_examples.scenario: A credible, named precedent exists (an RL benchmark paper's control-policy / oracle-baseline practice, or a sanity-check pattern already standard in NetHack Learning Environment or MiniHack) that does what SPAN or ARTIFACT does, undermining 'none of it is DF-specific' and 'nobody is auditing arenas' as the core differentiation claim — the instrument's novelty would be a naming/packaging difference, not a methodology gap.

severity_examples.condition: The reviewer can name the specific benchmark and explain concretely why no scripted-optimal analog exists there.
severity_examples.scenario: SPAN's core question ('can this metric see a perfect scripted policy') is unanswerable for at least one of the four named comparison classes because no scripted-optimal policy is constructible in that benchmark's action space — the 'portable to any agentic leaderboard' claim is false for at least one named target, not just untested.

severity_examples.condition: No filtering by activity/maintenance status is applied before the 134 figure is used to argue the audit gap is wide open.
severity_examples.scenario: The '134 repos, none auditing' competitive read treats an unfiltered denominator (including abandoned forks/demos) as if it represented active, serious competitive effort — inflates the apparent size of the gap without changing whether the gap is real among the repos that matter.

success_hints: Name specific existing benchmarks, papers, or repos (not 'some RL papers exist') when asserting a precedent — an unnamed claim of prior art is not falsifiable and won't move the review.
